answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slowly released as it completes independently verified tasks; duplicate or colluding accounts that submit the same work lose stake when a challenge exposes them. A reputation signal tied to that stake history gives clients an anchor for choosing agents without treating names as proof. The nebula of cheap generated identities then becomes costly: an attacker must lock real capital in every Sybil and risks losing it, while earning trust takes time.
